'''Giedrė Purvaneckienė''' (born 1945) is a Lithuanian politician and academic. She was one of the founders and initial instructors of the [[Women's studies|Women's Studies]] Centre in Vilnius. She served as the state advisor on women, children, and the family from 1994 to 2000 to the [[government of Lithuania]] and the [[United Nations Development Program]]. She was a member of the [[Seimas]] between 2001 and 2004 and 2012 to 2016. Purvaneckienė led the Lithuanian delegation of the [[Baltic Assembly]] between 2004 and 2005, before becoming president of the Assembly in 2015.

==Early life and education==
Giedrė Vazalinskaitė was born on 8 March 1945 in [[Kaunas]], [[Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic]] to [[Vytautas Vazalinskas]], a Lithuanian [[agronomist]] who was responsible for establishing agricultural testing stations and agrarian institutes throughout the country and served in the [[Supreme Soviet of the Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic]] from 1955 until his death in 1984.{{sfn|Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija|2011}}{{sfn|Švedienė|1996}} Vazalinskaitė was very close to her father as a child and remembered him as teaching she and her siblings how to ride a bicycle, skate and swim. He was a polyglot and also played the guitar.{{sfn|''Mano ūkis''|2010}}  After graduating from {{ill|Salomėja Nėris Gymnasium|lt=Vilnius Salomėja Nėris Secondary School|lt|Vilniaus Salomėjos Nėries gimnazija}} in 1963, she attended [[Vilnius University]] becoming a semiconductor physicist in 1968.{{sfn|Seimas|2016|p=Biografija}} After her graduation, in 1969, she married Raimundas Purvaneckas.{{sfn|Central Electoral Commission|2008}}{{sfn|Social Democratic Party of Lithuania|2013}}

==Career==
===Academia===
Between 1968 and 1973, Purvaneckienė worked as a junior research fellow for the [[Lithuanian Academy of Sciences]]. The following year, she became a laboratory assistant at Vilnius University, and was promoted in 1975 to head the teaching laboratory of their Institute of Semiconductors. In 1982, she earned her [[Candidate (degree)|candidate's degree]] in [[pedagogy]] from Vilnius University. Purvaneckienė was a research associate from 1986 through 1991 in the social sciences faculty. Simultaneously she taught as a senior [[lecturer]] between 1989 and 1994 and headed the department from 1991 to 1994.{{sfn|Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija|2011}}{{sfn|Seimas|2016|p=Biografija}} Purvaneckienė has completed several internships abroad, including at the [[University of Oslo]] in 1993, at the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1995, and at the [[University of Gothenburg]] in 1996. She became an associate professor at Vilnius University in 1995.{{sfn|Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija|2011}}{{sfn|''Mano ūkis''|2010}} That year, she became one of the founders and first instructors at the Women's Studies Centre in Vilnius.{{sfn|Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija|2011}}{{sfn|Pavilionienė|2015|pp=284-285}}

==Politics==
Purvaneckienė was active in the women's movement in Lithuania throughout the 1990s and was led through her activism into politics.{{sfn|Navickaitė|2019|p=234}} She served as the state advisor on women, children, and family matters between 1994 and 1997.{{sfn|Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija|2011}} During that time, she participated in the [[World Conference on Women, 1995|Fourth World Conference on Women]] held in [[Beijing]], China in 1995.{{sfn|Seimas|2016|p=Biografija}} From 1997 to 2000, she was an advisor on gender to the [[United Nations Development Program]] and published handbooks on women for the organization. In 1998, she joined the [[Social Democratic Party of Lithuania]] and the following year became vice chair of the party's women's caucus.{{sfn|Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija|2011}} The women's caucus worked to secure passage of the law on Equal Opportunities of Men and Women and national implementation plans for equality.{{sfn|Avdeyeva|2015|p=171}}

In 2000, Purvaneckienė was elected as a member of the [[Seimas]], Lithuania's parliament. She served as chair of the Family and Child Affairs Commission between 2001 and 2004 and in the latter year was appointed to lead the country's delegation to the [[Baltic Assembly]].{{sfn|Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija|2011}} Her term in politics ended in 2004 and she returned to teaching, until she was re-elected to the Seimas in 2012.{{sfn|Seimas|2016|p=Biografija}} In 2015, when Lithuania took over the presidency of the Baltic Assembly, she became President of the assembly.{{sfn|''Lithuania Tribune''|2015}}

==Research and selected works==
Purvaneckienė has published over sixty academic works.{{sfn|Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija|2011}}  Many of her works had to do with policies about education, women and family issues, such as the discrimination faced by working women.{{sfn|Stonkuvienė|2015|p=132}}
